return_model.question: Will an identified buyer place another positive-merchandise order within 90 days?

design.leakage_guard: features use only rows on or before each cutoff; the training label window ends before the test cutoff

limitations: Predicts observed repeat purchasing, not causal effects of any intervention.
Buyers without a customer identifier cannot be scored.
Base rates shift with the season (train 32% vs test 44%, the test window holds the Christmas peak), so probabilities are under-calibrated in the middle deciles; ranking (AUC) is the reliable output.
Scores at the reference day come from a refit on the most recent labelled window and have no held-out evaluation of their own.

value_at_risk.rule: identified buyers with predicted return probability < 33% at the reference day

anomalies.method: Expected = median net of the same weekday over the previous 8 observed weeks (needs 4). Robust z = 0.6745·(residual − median)/MAD; |z| > 3.5 flagged. Drivers are the day's largest lines.

weekday.test: Kruskal–Wallis H on observed-day net by ISO weekday

invoice_value.test: Mann–Whitney U, positive-merchandise invoice value, Dec 2010–Nov 2011 vs Dec 2009–Nov 2010
invoice_value.note: Invoices are not independent draws (repeat customers), so p-values are descriptive. Bootstrap resamples invoices.
